title: Indian-Origin Banker Rishi Madlani Enters Race for Keir Starmer's London Seat
excerpt: The sustainable finance executive and former Camden councillor is among several candidates vying for Labour's nomination in the Holborn and St Pancras by-election.
body:
• Rishi Madlani, a British banker of Indian-Ugandan heritage, is seeking Labour's candidacy to succeed former PM Keir Starmer as MP for Holborn and St Pancras
  • Starmer resigned his parliamentary seat on September 1, 2026, weeks after leaving Downing Street, triggering a high-profile by-election
  • Labour is fast-tracking candidate selection with a decision expected by September 9, while Green Party leader Zack Polanski plans to challenge for the seat
  • Madlani serves as UK Head of Sustainability at Investec and sits on the boards of RenewableUK and the UK Sustainable Investment and Finance Association

A High-Stakes By-Election Takes Shape

Rishi Madlani, a 44-year-old British banker of Indian origin, has thrown his hat into the ring for one of the most watched parliamentary races in recent British politics. The former Camden councillor is seeking the Labour Party's nomination to succeed Keir Starmer as MP for Holborn and St Pancras in central London, according to reports in The Times and Westminster Extra.

Starmer resigned his seat on September 1, weeks after handing the keys to 10 Downing Street to his successor Andy Burnham in July. The former prime minister told the Camden New Journal that he wanted to "pass the baton to a successor" and focus on international affairs, defence, and combating violence against women.

"It has been a huge honour and privilege to represent the best constituency in the country. I will now focus on other things, and that will be international affairs including defence, security, trade and technology in a fast-changing world."

— Keir Starmer, former Prime Minister

From Leicester to the London School of Economics

Madlani comes from Leicester's African Asian community. His mother was forced to leave Uganda in the 1970s during the mass expulsion of South Asians under Idi Amin's regime. He studied at the London School of Economics, where he rose to become General Secretary of the Students' Union.

In his professional career, Madlani serves as UK Head of Sustainability for Investec and Head of Sustainable Finance and Just Transition at NatWest Group. He sits on the boards of RenewableUK, UK100 — a network of local government leaders supporting climate action — and the UK Sustainable Investment and Finance Association.

He served as a councillor for Bloomsbury in Camden for twelve years from 2014, chairing the Pensions Committee and serving as the borough's LGBT+ champion. He lost his council seat in the May 2026 local elections to Green Party candidate Lilac Carr. He also previously sought the Labour candidacy for Leicester East ahead of the 2024 general election but lost to Rajesh Agrawal, a deputy mayor of London.

A Crowded Field and a Green Challenge

Madlani faces competition from within his own party. Other potential Labour candidates include Sagal Abdi-Wali, the Labour leader of Camden Borough Council; Adam Hug, former leader of Westminster City Council; and Nash Ali, a former Camden councillor and mayor, according to The Guardian. Former foreign secretary David Miliband was suggested as a candidate but declined, choosing to remain in New York where he leads the International Rescue Committee.

Labour is fast-tracking the selection process. Applications closed on September 4, with the candidate expected to be chosen on September 9 following interviews and a selection meeting.

The bigger challenge may come from across the political aisle. Green Party leader Zack Polanski announced on September 3 that he intends to stand in the by-election, with local Green members reportedly supportive of his candidacy. In the 2026 Camden council elections, the Green Party won 27.1% of the vote compared to Labour's 32.8%, signalling a genuine contest.

What It Means for the Diaspora

If selected and elected, Madlani would add to a growing cohort of British politicians with Indian heritage in Westminster. His personal story — rooted in the forced displacement of East African Asians and shaped by a career in sustainable finance — mirrors the arc of many in the diaspora who have channelled immigrant resilience into public service.

Madlani described himself as a close ally of Starmer. He won the Inspirational Leader Award at the 2022 British LGBT Awards and co-founded Foxes Pride, the LGBT+ supporters' association for Leicester City Football Club.

What's Next

Labour's candidate selection is expected by September 9. Once a candidate is chosen, the formal by-election process begins — the chief whip moves a writ in the Commons, and the statutory timetable runs for 21 to 27 working days from the writ's issue. No polling date has been set yet, but the contest is expected to be one of the most competitive by-elections of the parliament.
